# m.economy.labor_market

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

US labor-market indicators: unemployment, participation, earnings, and job openings.

Call it from a session `m`, made with `dm.MassiveSession()`:

```python
m.economy.labor_market(*, start=None, end=None, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

- [Methods](README.md#query-methods): `fetch()`, `poll(interval)`
- Read from: REST
- `poll()` by default: `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`, which holds only the latest poll's rows, one row per `Date`

[Dataset index](README.md)

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AvgHourlyEarnings` | double | Average hourly earnings of all employees on private nonfarm payrolls in USD (CES0500000003 series from FRED). |
| `Date` | String | Calendar date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `JobOpenings` | double | Total nonfarm job openings in thousands (JTSJOL series from FRED). |
| `LaborForceParticipationRate` | double | Civilian labor force participation rate as a percentage of the civilian noninstitutional population (CIVPART series from FRED). |
| `UnemploymentRate` | double | Civilian unemployment rate as a percentage of the labor force (UNRATE series from FRED). |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, by the local clock. Rows that arrive together share it. It isn't Massive's time, and later rows can carry earlier times. In a `poll()` table, it's the time of the poll the row's values came from. |
